name: Delay feature updates by 30 days
summary: Wait 30 days after release before a new Windows version is offered.
what: Applies the Windows Update policy that defers feature updates for 30 days.
benefit: Other people find the early problems first. Security updates still arrive on time.
risk: Low. New features arrive 30 days later than they would otherwise.
advice: Suggested if you want a month for early problems to be found and fixed before a new Windows version reaches you.
facts: Only feature updates are delayed, monthly security updates still install
You choose one delay, picking another replaces it
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education
Revert removes the policy values

name: Keep drivers out of Windows Update
summary: Windows Update will not install hardware drivers.
what: Applies the policy that excludes drivers from Windows quality updates.
benefit: No surprise driver swaps. Graphics, audio and network drivers stay what you chose.
risk: Low. You update drivers yourself from the maker or a tool you trust.
advice: Suggested for gamers and creators who install drivers from the vendor. Skip it if you rely on Windows to keep drivers current.
facts: Security and quality updates still install
Windows may offer older driver versions than the maker

Revert removes the policy value

name: Do not wake the PC for updates
summary: Windows Update will not wake a sleeping PC to install updates.
what: Applies the policy that turns off Windows Update power management wake up.
benefit: The PC stays asleep at night and does not wake to restart.
risk: None. Updates install when the PC is on.
facts: Updates still install, just not by waking the PC

name: Stop Edge from personalizing ads with your browsing
summary: Edge will not send browsing data to Microsoft to personalize ads, search and news.
what: Applies the Edge policy that stops sending browsing history, favorites and usage to Microsoft for personalization.
benefit: Your browsing is not used to personalize ads and services.
risk: None. Ads are not removed, they are just less personalized.
advice: Suggested for everyone who uses Edge.
facts: Not available for child or enterprise accounts
Users cannot change it while it is on
Revert removes the policy value

name: Hide the Edge sidebar
summary: Remove the launcher bar on the right side of Edge.
what: Applies the Edge policy that never shows the sidebar.
benefit: More room for pages and fewer built in shortcuts and promotions.
advice: Suggested if you never use the sidebar tools.
facts: Hides the sidebar for everyone who uses Edge on this PC
Edge may show that it is managed
Revert removes the policy value

name: Stop Edge from starting with Windows
summary: Edge will not preload itself at sign in.
what: Applies the Edge policy that turns startup boost off.
benefit: Less memory use at sign in and a lighter background footprint.
risk: Low. Edge may take a moment longer to open the first time.
advice: Suggested for everyone, especially if you use another browser.
facts: Startup boost keeps Edge processes ready in the background
Applies to every account
Revert removes the policy value

name: Stop Edge running after you close it
summary: Edge will fully quit when you close the last window.
what: Applies the Edge policy that turns background mode off.
benefit: No Edge process or tray icon after you close it.
risk: Low. Web apps and notifications from Edge stop when it is closed.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not rely on Edge web app notifications.
facts: Background mode keeps apps and session cookies alive after the window closes

name: Turn off Edge shopping features

benefit: No banners about coupons and prices, and fewer requests to shopping servers about the pages you visit.
